title: Invertible modules lift along a closed immersion into a Noetherian space of dimension at most one
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian (every nonempty set of closed subsets of $X$ has a minimal element for inclusion) and has Krull dimension $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then for every invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal N$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ with $i^*\mathcal L\cong\mathcal N$ as $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, $i^*$ the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]; that is, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$ is surjective.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 09NY (varieties-lemma-lift-line-bundle-from-reduction-dimension-1, line 8138); its proof uses Cohomology Proposition 02UZ (cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian), Cohomology Lemma 02UV (cohomology-lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions) and Cohomology Lemma 09NU (cohomology-lemma-h1-invertible)

proof.text: Let I be the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf defining the closed immersion i: Z \to X. The unit sheaves fit into the short exact sequence 0 \to (1 + I) \cap O_X^* \to O_X^* \to i_*O_Z^* \to 0, where the last map is restriction of units and the kernel consists exactly of units congruent to 1 modulo I.

source.place: Lemma 09NY, proof, opening displayed short exact sequence

proof.text: The underlying space of X is Noetherian and has dimension at most one by hypothesis. Applying [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-vanishing-abelian-dim-one] to the abelian sheaf (1 + I) \cap O_X^* gives H^2(X, (1 + I) \cap O_X^*) = 0. By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], the short exact sequence in step 1 has a long exact cohomology sequence, so H^1(X, O_X^*) \to H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 09NY, proof, sentences beginning 'Since dim(X) <= 1' and 'Hence the map'

proof.text: By [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] with p=1 and the sheaf O_Z^*, H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) is naturally isomorphic to H^1(Z, O_Z^*). Thus the surjection of step 2 is a surjection H^1(X, O_X^*) \to H^1(Z, O_Z^*).

source.place: Lemma 09NY, proof, sentence beginning 'By Cohomology, Lemma 02UV'

proof.text: The isomorphism between isomorphism classes of invertible modules and H^1 of the sheaf of units from [thm-sc-hilbert-90], applied to X and to Z, identifies H^1(X, O_X^*) and H^1(Z, O_Z^*) with Pic(X) and Pic(Z), respectively. By [lem-sc-picard-h1-restriction-compatibility], these identifications carry the map in step 3 to the pullback map L \mapsto i^*L. Hence the surjection in step 3 is the asserted surjection Pic(X) \to Pic(Z), so every invertible O_Z-module is isomorphic to the pullback of an invertible O_X-module.

source.place: Lemma 09NY, proof, final sentence 'This proves the lemma by Cohomology, Lemma 09NU'
